title: Check yourself: generic methods in enums

questions.stem: An enum `Column { ID, CREATED_AT }` declares `<T> T value(Map<String, Object> row)`, which returns `(T) row.get(name())`. In one method a developer writes `Instant at = Column.CREATED_AT.value(row);` and, two lines below, `String label = Column.CREATED_AT.value(row);`. What does javac do with these two lines?

options.text: It compiles both, since each call gets its own T from the variable its result is assigned to
options.says: a method's type parameter is inferred per call from the target type; nothing ties CREATED_AT to one type

options.text: It compiles both, since an unchecked cast inside value() switches off type checks for its callers
options.says: callers are still type-checked; both lines compile because T is inferred anew at each call, and the caller gets a checkcast

options.text: It rejects the String line, since the Instant line above it has already fixed T for CREATED_AT
options.says: a constant carries no type argument; T belongs to each call, not to the constant

options.text: It rejects the String line, since javac reads the type CREATED_AT holds from the values in the map
options.says: javac never sees the map's run-time contents; T comes from the call's target type

origin.section: An Enum Can't Take a Type Parameter, but Its Methods Can, and Each Call Picks T

questions.stem: An enum method `<T> List<T> values(Map<String, List<String>> props)` returns the stored list through an unchecked cast. At startup a service runs `List<Integer> sizes = Feature.SIZES.values(props);` while the stored list is `["10", "20"]`, and startup completes. Later a request handler evaluates `sizes.contains(10)`. What happens?

options.text: It returns false, since contains compares the strings with 10 and no cast check runs on that call
options.says: the cast compiled to nothing; contains takes an Object, so no checkcast runs and "10" is not equal to 10

options.text: It returns true, since the cast in values() turned each string into an Integer when it returned
options.says: a cast never converts a value; after erasure the cast to List<T> checks nothing at all

options.text: It throws ClassCastException in the handler, since a check runs on each element that contains reads
options.says: the compiler adds a check only where a value meets a concrete type in the caller, and contains(Object) hands back no element

options.text: It throws ClassCastException in values(), since the unchecked cast is checked once the list is used
options.says: an unchecked cast does no check where it is written, then or later; startup completed and values() is not running

origin.section: An Unchecked Cast Checks Nothing Where It Is Written

questions.stem: An enum's `<T> T load(String key, Class<T> type)` ends with `return type.cast(cache.get(key));`. The cache holds the `Long` 42 under "ttl". Two callers run `load("ttl", long.class)` and `load("ttl", Number.class)`. Which of the calls throw ClassCastException?

options.text: Only the long.class call, since no object is an instance of a primitive type
options.says: long.class has type Class<Long> and compiles, but isInstance is false for every object, so cast throws

options.text: Only the Number.class call, since cast accepts only the value's exact class
options.says: cast accepts any instance of the token's class, so a Long passes a Number token

options.text: Both calls, since cast accepts only the value's exact class and long.class is a different class
options.says: the Number call succeeds: cast accepts instances of subclasses

options.text: Neither call, since long.class and Number.class both accept a Long at run time
options.says: a primitive class token accepts no object, so the long.class call throws

origin.section: A `Class<T>` Token Makes the Cast Real, Inside the Method

questions.stem: A helper `<E extends Enum<E>> List<E> laterThan(E current)` reads `E[] all = (E[]) current.getClass().getEnumConstants();` and returns the constants after `current`. The enum is `Tier { FREE, PRO { @Override int seats() { return 5; } }, TEAM; int seats() { return 1; } }`. `laterThan(Tier.FREE)` returns `[PRO, TEAM]`. What does `laterThan(Tier.PRO)` do?

options.text: It throws NullPointerException, since PRO's class is a subclass that lists no enum constants
options.says: PRO with a body is an instance of an anonymous subclass; getEnumConstants() returns null for it

options.text: It throws ClassCastException, since the cast to E[] is checked when the array comes back
options.says: the array is null, and a null passes any cast; the failure comes when the null array is read

options.text: It returns [TEAM], since getClass() gives Tier for every constant Tier declares
options.says: only getDeclaringClass() gives Tier for every constant; getClass() of PRO is its anonymous subclass

options.text: It returns [], since PRO's own subclass declares no constants after PRO
options.says: getEnumConstants() on a class that isn't an enum returns null, not an empty array

origin.section: Spot the Problem: `getClass()` in Place of `getDeclaringClass()`
